land.text: Kismayo and its district, captured in August 2008

predecessors.note: Al-Shabaab grew out of the Islamic Courts Union's youth wing (2006) and first held a city in August 2008: 'In August 2008, Al-Shabaab and Islamic Courts Union fighters captured the southern port city of Kismayo' (Battle of Kismayo page). The Cliopatria shape of the Federal Republic of Somalia (1960-2023) covers all of Somalia and Somaliland, so every cell al-Shabaab held was nominally that state's.

correction.text: Kismayo and its district, captured in August 2008

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no row for al-Shabaab. Kismayo, captured in August 2008, is the first land the pages give; the 60 km disc is the researcher's reading of 'the southern port city'.

correction.text: most of central and southern Somalia, south of Puntland: Bakool, Bay, Gedo, Hiiraan, Middle and Lower Juba, Middle and Lower Shabelle and Galguduud (admin1 reading of the page's phrase), with the districts of Mogadishu (Banaadir) that al-Shabaab held

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'In 2009-2010 the group controlled most of central and southern Somalia, south of Puntland' (Al-Shabaab page); 'Al-Shabaab controlled roughly half the lands claimed by the Somali government at their greatest extent in 2009 July' (Somali Civil War page). The nine admin1 units are the researcher's reading (the pages name no region list except Bakool, Jowhar and Lower Juba) and probably overstate Galguduud and Gedo; Banaadir is a low-confidence addition (no page gives 2009 Mogadishu districts) and is contested from August 2010 by the ledger. Cliopatria's single Somalia shape (646,087 km2) is the whole of Somalia plus Somaliland, so there is no area to compare; the nine units resolve to about 325,000 km2, 62 per cent of the gazetteer's Somalia (523,250 km2) against the page's 'roughly half' in July 2009, so the reading is generous.

correction.text: most of central and southern Somalia, south of Puntland: Bakool, Bay, Gedo, Hiiraan, Middle and Lower Juba, Middle and Lower Shabelle and Galguduud (admin1 reading of the page's phrase) without Mogadishu (abandoned 6 August 2011) and Beledweyne (retaken 31 December 2011)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, as of 31 December 2011: al-Shabaab 'abandoned all areas in Mogadishu' on the night of 5 to 6 August 2011 (Daynile held to 20 October) and Beledweyne fell on 31 December 2011 (Operation Linda Nchi page).

correction.text: the rural south and centre after the loss of Beledweyne (Dec 2011), Baidoa (Feb 2012) and Kismayo (Oct 2012): 'still controls large swathes of territory in southern Somalia' and is 'influential in many rural areas'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: after Baidoa (February 2012) and Kismayo (October 2012) the group 'still controls large swathes of territory in southern Somalia' and 'remains influential in many rural areas' (Somali Civil War page, undated). The shape is the 2009-2010 core less the towns the pages date; towns not dated on the pages (Afgooye, Merca, Marka, Afmadow, Jowhar, Bardhere) are not cut out, so the shape is a generous rural reading (confidence 1).

correction.text: the same rural south and centre after Barawa was retaken in October 2014; Jilib (Middle Juba) is the headquarters from 2014 and the Jubba valley the base in 2020

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Barawa, a base in 2012-2014, was retaken in October 2014. Later dated changes (Bardhere and Dinsoor from 19 July 2015, Marka regained in 2016, the August 2022 Hiran offensive, 'one third' of its territory lost by March 2023, Mudug reversals to February 2024) are on the Somali Civil War page but without coordinates or boundaries, so they are not drawn; the keyframe is held to 2026 as a soft rural tint.

region.text: Kismayo and its district, captured in August 2008

ledger.note: August 2008: Al-Shabaab and Islamic Courts Union fighters capture Kismayo. 'In August 2008, Al-Shabaab and Islamic Courts Union fighters captured the southern port city of Kismayo.' The page does not say who held the city; the Somali government's shape is the counterpart on the grid.

region.text: Bakool province, where al-Shabaab 'launched an offensive' and took Hudur

ledger.note: February 2009: the Bakool offensive. 'An offensive was launched two days later by al-Shabaab to take the Bakool province'; 'al-Shabaab forces took the town of Hudor' around 24 February. The month is read from the page's neighbouring dates.

region.text: the districts of Mogadishu that al-Shabaab held until August 2011

ledger.note: May 2009: al-Shabaab and Hizbul Islam take most of Mogadishu. 'On 7 May, a fierce battle for control of Mogadishu started between al-Shabaab and Hizbul Islam against the TFG'; 'By 11 May, rebel forces gained the upper hand and made large gains taking over most of the capital.' In August 2011 al-Shabaab 'lost the significant control it had established in the city'. The whole Banaadir unit is the researcher's reading of 'most of the capital' (shared with Hizbul Islam). The contest from August 2010 follows. (Month and confidence set by reviewer n-mod from the page.)

region.text: Jowhar, the strategic town of Middle Shabelle

ledger.note: 16 May 2009: Jowhar falls. 'By 16 May, al-Shabaab captured the strategic town of Jowhar.'

region.text: most of central and southern Somalia, south of Puntland: Bakool, Bay, Gedo, Hiiraan, Middle and Lower Juba, Middle and Lower Shabelle and Galguduud (admin1 reading of the page's phrase)

ledger.note: July 2009 (month from the Somali Civil War page: 'at their greatest extent in 2009 July'; reviewer n-mod). 2009: al-Shabaab holds most of central and southern Somalia. 'The group controlled most of central and southern Somalia, south of Puntland, and built administrative structures to govern it' (2009-2010). The span is the page's; the nine regions are the researcher's reading. In July 2009 it held 'roughly half the lands claimed by the Somali government' (Somali Civil War page).

region.text: the Lower Juba region, from which Ahmad Madobe's forces were 'forced to withdraw'

ledger.note: November 2009: Lower Juba. Ahmad Madobe's forces 'were ultimately overpowered by al-Shabaab and its local allies, and forced to withdraw from the Lower Juba region and most of Southern Somalia'; on 1 October 2009 'al-Shabaab controlled most of the city' of Kismayo. The rival militia is not a dossier; the Somali government's shape is the grid counterpart.

region.text: Mogadishu, where the TFG and AMISOM fought al-Shabaab district by district

ledger.note: 23 August 2010: the Battle of Mogadishu begins (infobox 23 August 2010 to 20 October 2011); in October 2010 officials 'claimed that they had the upper hand in six of the capital's 16 districts'. Earlier fighting in the city is on no page opened.

region.text: Mogadishu, abandoned by al-Shabaab on the night of 5 to 6 August 2011

ledger.note: 6 August 2011: al-Shabaab leaves Mogadishu. 'During the night from Friday to Saturday, 6 August, al-Shabaab abandoned all areas in Mogadishu'; 'On 20 October AMISOM entered Daynile, the last district in Mogadishu that was under the control of al-Shabaab.' The Somali Civil War page: 'In August 2011, al-Shabaab withdrew from Mogadishu'.
August 2011: Mogadishu to the TFG and AMISOM; the Daynile remnant (a part of one cell) lasts to 20 October.

31 December 2011: Beledweyne falls. 'On 31 December 2011, the TFG retook control of Beledweyne from the Al-Shabaab militants', with about 3,000 allied Ethiopian troops. The Kenyan invasion of the south began in October 2011.
February 2012: Baidoa is lost. 'The group lost Baidoa to Ethiopia' (February 2012, Al-Shabaab page); the Somali Civil War page does not date it.

region.text: Kismayo, 'Al-Shabaab's last major stronghold', and its port

ledger.note: 1 October 2012: Kismayo falls. Al-Shabaab 'officially pulled out of the town' on 29 September and Somali government soldiers 'entered Kismayo's center on 1 October 2012' after the Kenyan and Ras Kamboni landing north of the city on 28 September; the port was the group's revenue base (charcoal and taxes).

October 2014: Barawa is retaken. 'The Somali Armed Forces assisted by AMISOM troops re-seized control of Barawa from Al-Shabaab in October 2014'; 'In 2009, Al-Shabaab militants seized control of Barawa'. The disc's coordinates are the researcher's.

wars.name: Somali Civil War (2009-present)

zones.text: most of central and southern Somalia, south of Puntland: Bakool, Bay, Gedo, Hiiraan, Middle and Lower Juba, Middle and Lower Shabelle and Galguduud (admin1 reading of the page's phrase)

wars.outcome: Al-Shabaab held about half the government's claimed land in July 2009, was driven from Mogadishu (August 2011), Baidoa (February 2012) and Kismayo (October 2012), and kept large rural areas of the south; by March 2023 it had 'lost one third of its territory' since the August 2022 offensive and in April 2025 recaptured Adan Yabaal.
wars.note: The page's dated list runs to 2025; only the dated changes with a nameable place are in the ledger.

wars.name: Battle of Mogadishu (2010-2011)
wars.outcome: TFG and AMISOM victory: al-Shabaab abandoned the city on 6 August 2011 and the last district, Daynile, was cleared on 20 October 2011.
wars.note: Infobox dates 23 August 2010 to 20 October 2011; the Ramadan offensive of August 2010 'failed with heavy losses' (Al-Shabaab page).

wars.name: Operation Linda Nchi
wars.outcome: Kenyan forces (re-hatted under AMISOM in early June 2012), the TFG and Ras Kamboni took Qoqani (17 October 2011), Afmadow (31 May 2012) and, on 28 September 2012, launched the amphibious offensive on Kismayo; Ethiopia and the TFG retook Beledweyne on 31 December 2011.
wars.note: Afmadow (31 May 2012) is not drawn: the gazetteer has no point for it and the page gives no coordinates.

wars.name: Battle of Kismayo (2012)
wars.outcome: Kenyan-Somali victory: 28 September to 1 October 2012; al-Shabaab withdrew on 29 September and the government entered the centre on 1 October.
wars.note: Infobox: 'Kenyan and Raskamboni forces capture city on 1 October'.

certainty.note: Control moved by town and road and the pages give towns, not lines; rural control is 'semi-territorial' (the page's word for the group's presence since 2016) and only the dated towns are sharp.

notes: Written by n-mod from seven pages (two over the five-page budget: Barawa and Jilib only for two capitals and one town). REBEL STATE: Cliopatria has no row. COUNTERPART CONVENTION: every gain and loss names federal-republic-of-somalia because the Cliopatria shape of that state (1960-2023, 646,087 km2) is the whole of Somalia plus Somaliland and no other dossier holds the cells; the actual opponent (the TFG, AMISOM, Ethiopia, Kenya, Ras Kamboni, Ahmad Madobe's forces) is in each note. The federal-republic-of-somalia ledger has no matching loss events (it has 7 events and none of 2008-2014); a gap-filler should add them or the compile should treat this dossier's gains as taken from that shape. NOT SETTLED: (1) the extent of 2009-2010 control is the page's sentence only; the nine-region reading overstates Galguduud and parts of Gedo and Hiiraan; (2) Mogadishu 2009 to August 2010 (no page opened); (3) town-level changes after 2012 (Afgooye, Merca, Marka 2016, Bardhere and Dinsoor 2015, Afmadow May 2012, Jowhar) need coordinates the pages do not give; (4) Hizbul Islam / Ras Kamboni (Ahmad Madobe) are rivals that held Lower Juba until November 2009 and may need a small dossier; (5) the 'semi-territorial' keyframe 2012-2026 is a confidence-1 reading, and the rendering agents may prefer to end the dossier's tint at 2012. GAZETTEER NAMES NEEDED: Baraawe (Barawa), Jilib, Afmadow. End 2026 = alive today; no dissolve.
